content_of_post_to_answer: How do you tell the difference between a temporary change caused by fear and a permanent change in your character?
answer: A useful distinction is whether the change survives when the threat disappears. Fear can make us withdraw, become cautious, or abandon parts of ourselves because our mind is trying to protect us. Character changes are usually quieter: they show up repeatedly even when there is no pressure forcing them. A frightened version of you asks, “How do I stay safe?” A changed version of you asks, “What kind of person do I choose to be?” The test is not the intensity of the moment, but the pattern that remains after the moment passes.
